description: Share of the product mass saved by the RAW optimisation, compared with the non-optimised product given by the product size formula: product mass = formula x (1 - material_savings / 100)
source: No separate optimisation saving: the design rows (depth_ratio, width_ratio, density) carry the design uncertainty of the beam.
comments: [2026-10-16] Added: material savings as a parameter.

description: Beam span / beam depth (depth = span / depth_ratio)
source: Rule of thumb span/depth ~20 for timber beams (same value and range as the glulam baseline).
comments: DESIGN UNCERTAINTY: a better design (dowel placement and number, layer build-up, piece grading from the CT scan) can reach the same stiffness/strength with a shallower beam (higher ratio = less material), a worse one needs a deeper beam. At 6 m span: depth 0.25-0.375 m (typical 0.30 m, ~7 layers of 40 mm pieces).

description: Beam depth / beam width (width = depth / width_ratio)
source: Partners: pieces are stacked in depth only, so the beam width = one planed piece (~95 mm, partners' image). 0.30 m depth / 0.095 m = 3.2.
comments: DESIGN UNCERTAINTY: choosing wider or narrower reclaimed stock changes the width for the same depth. Range 2.5-4 = ~120 mm to ~75 mm wide at 0.30 m depth. Was 3 (2.4-3.6, placeholder).

description: Density of the reclaimed timber
source: Reclaimed European softwood (spruce/pine); C24 mean density ~420 kg/m3 (EN 338, general knowledge, not re-checked); old slow-grown timber is often denser. Opalis: reclaimed structural softwood mostly pine.
comments: DESIGN UNCERTAINTY: material selection. Lighter, weaker stock (420) vs denser, stronger old-growth stock (550). Note: in this simple model denser timber gives a heavier beam; the depth_ratio range carries the fact that stronger stock allows a smaller section. | [2026-10-16] Range 384-576 -> 432-528: reclaimed softwood ~430-530 kg/m3 (+-10 %)

description: Share of the production input mass made of this material (recycled = reclaimed); the shares of one stage add up to 100 %
source: Partners: reclaimed timber pieces; Opalis: reclaimed structural timber in Europe is mostly pine/spruce.
comments: Reclaimed softwood (was "Hard wood, recycled" 100%, placeholder). 99% = everything except the dowels. Fixed on purpose: uncertainty on this sheet is limited to the product-size parameters (design) and the planing yield (piece selection) (Tanya, 2026-09-30). | [2026-10-16] Range 79.2-118.8 -> 98-100: typical centred, range kept within 0-100 %

description: Share of the production input mass made of this material (virgin); the shares of one stage add up to 100 %
source: Partners: ~6 dowels of ~1 inch (25 mm) per beam, material unknown -> new softwood (Tanya).
comments: Dowels: 12 dowels per 6 m beam (2 per m, assuming the partners' 6 dowels were for a ~3 m beam), 25 mm diameter, running through the full depth: dowel volume / beam volume = 2 x 0.00049 m2 / 0.095 m = ~1%. No glue. Note: the model applies shares at the first step, so the dowels are also counted as scanned and planed (negligible). Fixed on purpose: uncertainty on this sheet is limited to the product-size parameters (design) and the planing yield (piece selection) (Tanya, 2026-09-30).

description: Electric power the machine draws while running
source: PROTOTYPE machinery: medical/lab X-ray CT scanner (partners) scanning 3-4 pieces at once at 1 min per 2 m.
